item.content:encoded: I love the concept, but not the execution. The containment is excessive on the personnel part, the description lags more than needed, and the addenda just seems out of purpose. They took too much space to show characteristics that should have been described in the, well, description, all the while with a testing that I can't imagine getting anything even near an approval.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I don't feel that either of the incident logs are particularly well explained. Why harvest it with chainsaws instead of just stripping some bark, or drilling out some small core samples?

Why did the tree fall without any further impetus, after the damage was healed?

Also, both of those expungements are just awful. There's no indication what's behind them and that really bothers me on any article.

Apart from those, the concept is beautiful, and I like the idea that maybe this copse of trees is where humans got the idea for something like a pipe organ. It's a -1 for the issues I have, but barely.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This SCP has not gotten the love it deserves. One of my favorites. It's so weird and kinda beautiful, it really nails the feeling you get when looking through an abandoned house or walking down an empty street at night, which is something I wish this wiki had more of.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I mean that the trunk didn't stand itself back up — it just healed as it was, leaning on its neighbor.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I like it. One minor thing, there's a reference to the organism not "righting" itself after a trunk was cut down although the trunk was noted to have healed. The verb "right" generally means to stand back up something that has been knocked down. Do you mean that the trunk was crooked? Or that it didn't replace the fallen trunk?

It's unique, it's mysterious, it's cool, it's strange, it's moderately creepy (trees with sphincters), and very original.
